note: Scripture authority is the Open Word Bible (OWB), Amharic, Balanced edition (CC0), bundled as library/data/bible/owb-am-b.json.gz and read offline (owb-am). Every Scripture quotation in this book was re-quoted to it verbatim (founder decision, 2026-11-18: Amharic quotes OWB everywhere), replacing the 1962/2003 UBS New Testament wording and the Old Testament wording borrowed from other Amharic works that the first edition carried; the UBS credit line this file once owed is no longer owed for this work.

A `mined` row is a verbatim OWB span in that block: the whole verse, verses joined, the shortest contiguous span carrying the quoted clause, or exact OWB pieces joined with '…'; a verbatim recitation without quote marks counts (founder rule, 2026-11-19). Quotations split across two blocks (Matthew 25:21 in chapter 11 blocks 34-35; Proverbs 19:17 opening at the end of block 27) are OWB across the join. `self_rendered` rows each carry a `why`: allusions and Allen's own paraphrases left as prose, and verses recast to another person.

Judgement calls: Acts 17:26 — OWB reads «ከአንድ ሰው» (from one man) where Allen's anti-slavery appeal rests on 'made of one blood', so his clause is rendered from the English and self_rendered (critical-text decision). Psalm 68:31 keeps ኢትዮጵያ (founder rule; OWB reads ኩሽ). Matthew 25:40 and 25:45 are joined with '…' under Allen's single conflated quotation. 2 Corinthians 1:20 quotes OWB's first sentence, which carries 'yea' but places 'Amen' in the next sentence, so Allen's 'yea and amen' reads as OWB's «አዎን». Psalm 41:1-3 is OWB's plural and 'the weak' (ለደካሞች) where the AV has 'the poor'.
